players.product: SMR designer (Xe-100) - Doosan Enerbility equity stake and prospective equipment customer

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Daniel Gross (first quarter reported as X-Energy Inc.; IPO closed the last week of April): Q2 2026 total revenues and grant income were $54.6 million, up 154% year over year - $50.1 million of services revenue, primarily Xe-100 design work under the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP), plus $4.5 million of grant income, primarily tied to the Dow demonstration reactor; total operating expenses were $164.6 million (direct costs $86.7 million, SG&A $77.7 million including $33.5 million of non-cash equity-based compensation), up 156%. Interest income was $11 million and other expense $6.3 million, mostly a non-cash $5.6 million mark-to-market loss on a warrant exercised in April, for total other income of a positive $4.7 million. Operating activities used $97.3 million (versus $20 million in Q2 2025), including significant prepayments to vendors on long lead materials; capital expenditures were $63.3 million for construction projects including TX-1, for which ARDP reimbursed $23.5 million in cash. Cash and investments were $1.9 billion at June 30, 2026 ($1.1 billion cash and cash equivalents, $490 million short-term and $265 million long-term investments), with zero debt outstanding.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenues and grant income $54.6 million (+154%); operating expenses $164.6 million; cash and investments $1.9 billion

quarterly_data.signal: ARDP funding (CEO Clay Sell): X-Energy has been allocated approximately $1.1 billion to date under the Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program, a 50/50 public-private partnership for its first commercial plant with Dow in Seadrift, Texas, and the DOE grant award is its largest source of revenue at its current stage. The Department of Energy formally notified X-Energy the day before the call that the ARDP cooperative agreement will receive up to an additional $1 billion, under the same 50/50 cost share and expected to be obligated through the normal contractual process, which would raise DOE's cost-share contribution to up to $2.115 billion. The cost share covers the Xe-100 reference plant design, the design, construction and licensing of the TX-1 fuel plant and the full project cost of the Dow deployment (CEO); it does not cover TX-2, TXL or later fuel facilities (CFO). As of June 30, 2026 DOE had reimbursed $547 million under the program. The CEO says X-Energy has not disclosed the full cost of the program and is confident further funding would be provided if required.
quarterly_data.figure: additional up to $1 billion; DOE cost share up to $2.115 billion; $547 million reimbursed as of June 30, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Fuel supply (CEO Clay Sell): for the first core loads at Dow, X-Energy has secured about 7.6 metric tons of existing material from the Department of Energy, and in the week before the call it executed binding long-term agreements for HALEU enrichment services with Centrus Energy and General Atomics, with firm delivery commitments growing in phases in line with its commercial pipeline (timing, quantities and pricing not disclosed by contract). Including the DOE allocation, it now has firm agreements covering the fuel needs for the initial and replacement core loads of its announced Xe-100 projects and beyond, which he says significantly reduces HALEU supply risk. Each Xe-100 starts on an LEU core, with HALEU from the second core onward; the HALEU for Dow will be available toward the end of the decade. X-Energy intends to transfer these fuel obligations to its customers at the appropriate stage of each project.
quarterly_data.figure: about 7.6 metric tons of DOE material

quarterly_data.signal: Graphite and components (CEO Clay Sell): under an agreement with SGL Carbon, X-Energy will invest up to $8 million in milestone-based payments for new facilities and equipment upgrades at SGL's Chedde, France facility; full execution would double SGL's medium grain graphite manufacturing capacity by 2030, enough graphite billets for up to eight new Xe-100 reactors per year. Other graphite types used in the reactor are also a focus, and further capacity-securing agreements are in the works.
quarterly_data.figure: up to $8 million; graphite for up to eight Xe-100 reactors per year by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: TRISO-X fuel (CEO Clay Sell): the NRC granted the Part 70 commercial license in February 2026 for an initial 40-year term (which he calls the first new commercial fuel fabrication facility licensed by the NRC in over 50 years). TX-1, built under a 50/50 DOE cost share and awarded up to $148 million in federal tax credits, has throughput for 11 Xe-100s; its vertical construction is about 80% complete and on track for the third-quarter milestone, after which interior build-out (graphite matrix powder building, utilities, equipment) begins. TX-2, covered by the same license and in the design phase, is expected to have four times TX-1's capacity and to be needed in the early 2030s (no construction or financing decision announced); a $11 million Tennessee grant supports TX-2 and the TXL R&D center, and the Oak Ridge campus would support fuel for approximately 55 Xe-100s. X-Energy acquired 70 adjacent acres in July (about 180 acres in total) and extended its CRADA with Oak Ridge National Laboratory; its pilot plant has consistently achieved greater than 95% first pass yield on kernel conversion.
quarterly_data.figure: TX-1 about 80% complete; TX-1 capacity 11 Xe-100s; TX-2 4x TX-1; up to $148 million tax credits

quarterly_data.signal: Project milestones (CEO Clay Sell): for the Dow Seadrift construction permit, X-Energy expects the NRC staff to close all safety questions by the end of August, final review in late 2026 and issuance by the first quarter of 2027. The Energy Northwest project in Washington State is expected to be its second project online and the first of 5 GW of new power projects with Amazon, with Energy Northwest moving toward construction permit submission in the first half of 2027. On the plan to announce the next 1 GW project in 2026, X-Energy is 'in the final throes of an agreement with a major investor-owned utility', with a full announcement in the near future; the long-term milestone roadmap into the early 2030s is unchanged.
quarterly_data.figure: Dow construction permit issuance by Q1 2027; Energy Northwest permit submission H1 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and pipeline (CEO Clay Sell): 'We are focused on that $2.3 trillion TAM that we can access with the Xe-100 and our TRISO fuel business' (a revenue potential he introduced from third-party estimates of the SMR market to 2050); announced customers are Dow, Amazon, Energy Northwest and the U.K. utility Centrica. He reports robust discussions with IPPs, investor-owned utilities, industrial customers, hyperscalers and foreign utilities, some in later phases of site feasibility review, and says the focus stays on the Xe-100 and TRISO-X fuel rather than the DoD Janus program. Inside the company, X-Energy joined DOE's Project Prometheus as a founding member (with organizations including Idaho National Laboratory, NVIDIA and Amazon Web Services), providing $10 million of private capital and its reactor-design and fuel-fabrication data for a three-year AI research campaign, and uses its internal multi-agentic AI platform APEX across engineering, licensing and operations.
quarterly_data.figure: $2.3 trillion TAM (CEO, from third-party SMR market estimates); $10 million to Project Prometheus
